subject.title: Sub-agent timeout recovery creates duplicate API posts (idempotency gap)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core durable logical-action idempotency and replay contract for sub-agent side effects, and what identity boundary should it use?
rationale: The remaining gap spans sub-agent lifecycle, Gateway idempotency, and arbitrary tool/API side effects; choosing the wrong identity could either duplicate committed effects or suppress legitimate repeated actions.

options.title: Design a narrow core contract
options.body: Define logical action identity, payload digest, target scope, expiry, completed-result replay, and audit semantics first, then implement the smallest core/Gateway change.

options.title: Limit core to exact-key dedupe
options.body: Treat current Gateway exact-key dedupe and message-tool mitigation as the core guarantee while workflows/plugins own external API idempotency.

options.title: Route operators to ClawHub guidance
options.body: Keep core unchanged and document that unattended multi-agent deployments must use workflow-level or service-level idempotency.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define logical action identity, payload digest, target scope, expiry, completed-result replay, and audit semantics first, then implement the smallest core/Gateway change.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent work on subagent registry persistence and completion handoffs makes this the best available owner for the durable lifecycle decision.
